purpose: Local 3D terrain for an oblique overview of each site. Visual geometry only: horizons and metrics come from sites/*.json (5 m near field plus 80 m and 240 m far field), not from these tiles.
encoding: Raw little-endian int16, row-major, metres above the 1737.4 km reference sphere (radius = 1737400 + value). No no-data values.

grid.projection: south polar stereographic on the 1737.4 km sphere, true scale at the pole; X/Y in metres; longitude 0 toward +Y, 90 E toward +X (same as manifest sites[].polarStereoXYM)
grid.cellCentre: x = xMin + (c + 0.5) * cellSizeM ; y = yMax - (r + 0.5) * cellSizeM (row 0 is the +Y edge, column 0 the -X edge)
grid.registration: cell-centred (PixelIsArea); the site lies on the shared corner of the four central cells
grid.aggregation: each cell = mean of 8 x 8 bilinear samples (5 m spacing) of the PGDA 5 m DEM; cells not fully covered by it use PDS LDEM_80S_80M bilinear at the cell centre (see fractionFromPgda5m)
grid.frame: MOON_ME of DE421 (same as all DEMs here)

helpers.toLatLon: rho = hypot(x, y); lat = -90 + 2 * atan(rho / (2 * 1737400)) [deg]; lon = atan2(x, y) [deg east]
helpers.toBodyFixedM: P = (1737400 + h) * (cos lat cos lon, cos lat sin lon, sin lat) in MOON_ME; use exact positions, not a flat plane (the drop is about 29 m at 10 km from the site)
helpers.toSiteENU: zenith U = unit(lat0, lon0); east E = normalize((0,0,1) x U); north N = U x E; local = ((P - O)·E, (P - O)·N, (P - O)·U) with O = (1737400 + h0) * U
helpers.mapAxesAtSite: at the site, map +rho (direction (sin lon0, cos lon0) in X/Y) is local north and (cos lon0, -sin lon0) is local east; the stereographic scale factor here is 1.000 to within 0.2%
helpers.normals: build normals from the exact 3D positions of neighbouring cells (cross product of central differences), not from the int16 values alone
helpers.threeMapping: same P mapping as sky.json and the globe: three (x, y, z) = (X_body, Z_body, -Y_body)

verticalScale: 1.0 (true scale). Any exaggeration must be labelled visual only.

source.near: PGDA High-Resolution LOLA Topography for Lunar South Pole Sites, 5 m/pix (Barker et al. 2021), https://pgda.gsfc.nasa.gov/products/78
